subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and where should the boundary sit between silent-intent internal text and legitimate substantive replies that append or mention the token?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally preserve some substantive trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; changing that shared delivery contract requires product/security intent.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define one shared silent-intent classifier that suppresses internal or status preambles but preserves legitimate substantive replies, then apply it across reply normalization, outbound delivery, cron, and streaming paths.

options.title: Use blanket trailing or own-line suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line NO_REPLY token, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, and reasoning-prefixed silent payloads are suppressed, then close broad suppression requests as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define one shared silent-intent classifier that suppresses internal or status preambles but preserves legitimate substantive replies, then apply it across reply normalization, outbound delivery, cron, and streaming paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a shared reply-delivery and security/product policy choice, and history shows steipete carried recent classifier follow-up work in the central files.
